name: Washoku Home
tagline: Dashi, bento, ramen and sushi in a home kitchen
about: Washoku Home makes everyday Japanese cooking approachable: dashi and miso soup, weeknight ramen bowls, safe sushi at home, next-day bento from leftovers and a label decoder for the Japanese grocery aisle.
persona: You are a Japanese home-cooking teacher rooted in washoku principles (seasonality, dashi, balance of five tastes) who gives grams and millilitres, is honest about what a home kitchen can and cannot do, and takes raw-fish safety seriously.

onboarding.title: Everyday Japanese cooking, simplified
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us what's in your pantry and your gear; recipes adapt to it.
bullets: Dashi and miso soup that tastes like Japan

tools.title: Dashi & miso soup
tools.subtitle: The base of everything, then 3 soups

inputs.label: In the fridge
inputs.placeholder: tofu, spring onion, half a daikon

tools.prompt: Teach {dashi} dashi, then miso soup using {fridge}, adapted to the profile's pantry. Sections: kv (water ml, kombu grams, katsuobushi or alternative grams, temperature ceiling, steep minutes, keeps for), steps for the dashi with the 'do not boil kombu' cue and the moment to pull it, cards for 3 miso soup variations from the fridge items (meta = miso type · minutes), and bullets on storing dashi and reusing spent kombu.

tools.title: Sushi at home
tools.subtitle: Rice, vinegar mix, and what fish is safe

inputs.label: Fish or fillings available
inputs.placeholder: supermarket salmon, tinned tuna, cucumber, avocado

tools.prompt: Plan {style} for {people} people with: {fish}. Sections: kv (rice grams, water ml, sushi-zu vinegar/sugar/salt in grams, cooling method), steps for rice and assembly using the profile's rice gear, a table 'Fillings' (Item | Safe raw? Yes/No/Only if labelled sashimi-grade or previously frozen | Prep | Cut), and a callout on raw-fish safety: freezing for parasites, sourcing, time out of the fridge, and who should avoid raw fish.

tools.title: Ramen bowl builder
tools.subtitle: Weeknight or weekend project
tools.prompt: Build a {broth} ramen in the '{time}' format for the profile's diet and pantry. Sections: a table 'Components' (Component | How to make it | Make-ahead? | Store for), steps for the assembly order and timing so noodles never sit, bullets of 5 toppings ranked by effort-to-payoff, and a callout on ajitama (marinated egg) timing and on where a shortcut is fine versus where it shows.

tools.title: Decode a Japanese label
tools.subtitle: Photo → what it is and how to use it
tools.prompt: Read the Japanese product label in the photo. Sections: kv (product name in romaji and English, category, key ingredients, common allergens present such as wheat/soy/fish/sesame, shelf life after opening), bullets on how it is used in Japanese cooking with amounts per serving, a table 'Compared to' (Similar product | Difference | Swap ratio), and a callout if it contains alcohol, MSG, gluten or fish that a vegetarian or allergy-aware user should know about.

tools.title: Bento from leftovers
tools.subtitle: Tomorrow's box from tonight's dinner
tools.prompt: Turn {leftovers} into a {style} bento. Sections: cards for 3 bento layouts (meta = minutes tomorrow morning · needs reheating yes/no), steps for assembly in the order that keeps rice from steaming the box, a checklist of what to prep tonight versus pack in the morning, and a callout on food safety for a box eaten cold at noon (cooling, acid, no mayo in heat).

disclaimer: General cooking guidance, not food-safety or dietary advice: follow safe handling, storage and allergen practices, take care with hot oil, open flames, raw or undercooked foods and fermentation, and discard anything that smells or looks wrong.
